context.description: Facts enter only through the Recorder, in one order

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review at HEAD 5fb09be29c; test unchanged since 6841bc0e5d; trial bun test 5 pass 0 fail. Given two supervisors that record facts at the same moment: test 1 runs the real TaskSupervisor machines of T1.1 and T1.2 (building, hanging turns) on one SimulatedClock, so one 2 s increment fires both stall timers and both record task.stalled through their real record workers, three rounds; test 2 fires 40 record-worker calls for the two tasks with unbounded concurrency. When the Recorder stores and folds them: the real TaskRecorder (permit + uninterruptible publish-then-send) over the real event store and run actor. Then store order equals fold order and times never decrease: stored facts are read back by durable sequence (TaskEvents.read) and compared entry by entry with the run actor's log since the slice (unit, reason and at, all in order; reasons unique in the burst), plus a non-decreasing check of stored at; 6 and 40 facts each present once. And a record after the run is done stores nothing: test 3 records run.cancelled (snapshot status done, run state cancelled); a stall queued behind it, both supervisors' later stall records and a later task.failed record all succeed without failure yet the store holds only run.cancelled and the fold log is unchanged. And an interrupted record leaves the whole fact or nothing: test 4 interrupts a record queued on the permit (exit interrupted; neither stored nor folded) and a record inside a held store write (the interrupt waits; the whole fact is stored and folded); test 5 interrupts 30 records at random moments and requires stored list == folded list. The held store wraps only EventV2 publish at the store boundary; the Recorder is real. Every step is asserted specifically.
